holidays.name: National Café au Lait Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the creamy, comforting French classic: strong brewed coffee mixed with warm steamed milk. Make one at home, order one at your favorite café, and sip slowly while pretending you're at a Parisian sidewalk table.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has been celebrated on February 17 in recent years by coffee lovers.
holidays.funFact: Café au lait is not a latte. Traditional café au lait uses brewed coffee, while a latte uses espresso. In France, the drink is typically served at breakfast in a wide bowl.

holidays.name: Random Acts of Kindness Day
holidays.description: A day for doing small, unexpected good deeds for friends and strangers. Pay for someone's coffee, leave an encouraging note, or hold the door open with extra flair.
holidays.origin: The Random Acts of Kindness Foundation was founded in the US in 1995. A kindness day began in New Zealand in 2004, and the observance is now marked on February 17 in the US.
holidays.funFact: New Zealand marks its own Random Acts of Kindness Day on a different date, September 1, so the kindness has more than one chance to spread.

holidays.name: World Human Spirit Day
holidays.description: A day for quiet reflection on the spirit inside us all. People are invited to pause, meditate, and think about freedom, peace, and the big questions without needing all the answers.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance that encourages people to take a moment of silence, with a popular suggestion of two minutes of meditation at 3 p.m. Eastern Time.
holidays.funFact: The celebration's signature move is only two minutes long, which makes it one of the shortest holidays to observe.
